questions.stem: Ivy says: 'We should walk to school instead of driving. It will help us get fitter.' Which statement most strengthens her argument?

options.B: The school has a big car park.
options.C: Ivy's friend lives next to the school.
options.D: Walking to school would add 40 minutes of exercise to each day.

questions.explanation: Extra daily exercise directly supports 'it will help us get fitter'.

distractors.B: doesn't help the argument about fitness

questions.stem: A sign says: 'Swimmers must stay between the flags.' Ben says: 'The flags are there, so the beach must be safe everywhere.' What is the mistake?

options.B: The flags show where it is safe; they don't mean everywhere is safe.
options.D: Flags blow away in the wind.

questions.explanation: The flags mark the safe area. That doesn't make the rest of the beach safe.

distractors.A: he's misunderstanding it, not failing to read it

questions.stem: All the students in the robotics club are in Year 5 or Year 6. Ari is in the robotics club. Which must be true?

options.A: Ari is in Year 5 or Year 6.
options.D: All Year 6 students are in the robotics club.

questions.explanation: Everyone in the club is in Year 5 or 6, so Ari is in one of those years.

distractors.D: the rule only goes one way

questions.stem: 'Our new café must be popular, because there was a long queue on opening day.' Which statement most weakens this?

options.C: Everything was free on opening day.

questions.explanation: Free food explains a queue without showing the café will stay popular.

questions.stem: Tia says: 'I got 100% on my spelling test, so I'll get 100% on my maths test.' What has Tia assumed?

options.B: She studied for the spelling test.
options.C: Doing well in spelling means she will do well in maths.

questions.explanation: She is linking two different subjects without any reason.

distractors.A: she doesn't mention how easy it is
distractors.D: not what her conclusion depends on

questions.stem: No reptiles have fur. All snakes are reptiles. Which must be true?

options.C: All animals without fur are reptiles.

questions.explanation: Snakes are reptiles, and no reptile has fur, so no snake has fur.

distractors.C: frogs and fish have no fur either

questions.stem: 'Since the council put in speed bumps, there have been fewer accidents on Elm Street. So the speed bumps are working.' Which statement most strengthens this?

options.A: Accidents on nearby streets without speed bumps have not gone down.
options.B: Elm Street has a school on it.
options.D: Some drivers don't like speed bumps.

questions.explanation: If other streets didn't improve, it's more likely the speed bumps caused the drop.

questions.stem: Lena: 'Everyone who came to my party had fun. Max had fun today, so he must have come to my party.' What is the mistake?

options.A: Max could have had fun somewhere else.

questions.explanation: Having fun doesn't prove he was at the party: people can have fun in many places.

questions.stem: Some of the books on the shelf are about space. All the books on the shelf are hardcovers. Which must be true?

options.A: Some hardcover books are about space.
options.C: All hardcover books are about space.
options.D: None of the books are about animals.

questions.explanation: The space books on the shelf are hardcovers, so some hardcovers are about space.

distractors.B: only the ones on this shelf

questions.stem: 'Kids should be allowed phones at school because they need them in emergencies.' Which statement most weakens this?

options.C: The school office can call parents straight away in an emergency.

questions.explanation: If the school already handles emergencies, the reason given isn't strong.

distractors.D: wanting isn't a reason linked to emergencies

questions.stem: 'My plant died, so I must have given it too much water.' What has the speaker assumed?

options.D: Too much water is the only reason the plant could have died.

questions.explanation: Plants can die for many reasons (too little water, pests, sun). The speaker picks one without checking.

questions.stem: At a fair, every ride costs at least $3. Noor has exactly $8. Which must be true?

options.A: Noor can go on at most 2 rides.
options.C: Noor can go on exactly 2 rides.

questions.explanation: With rides costing $3 or more, $8 is enough for at most 2 (3 rides would need at least $9).

distractors.C: if rides cost $5, she could only go on 1
